commentary: Sweden's spring 2026 budget package arrives as the economy climbs out of a 2023 contraction: GDP grew 0.82% in 2024 after shrinking 0.20% in 2023, while inflation fell sharply to 2.84% in 2024 from the 8.55% peak in 2023. Yet the recovery remains uneven — unemployment has risen to 8.7% in 2025, up from 8.4% in 2024, meaning roughly 450,000 Swedes remain out of work even as prices stabilize. The Extra ändringsbudget fuel and energy subsidies (HD03236) directly respond to the cost-of-living shock that drove inflation to a four-decade high in 2022-23, but economists note that subsidizing fossil fuels when Sweden's fiscal position is already under supplementary-budget pressure risks undermining the credibility of the fiscal framework reviewed in Riksrevisionens rapport (HD03241).
